facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He feels like he is running on fumes.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work stress and workload
facts.content: Daniel works as a project manager at a logistics company. He has been doing three people's jobs since losing a client.
facts.evidence: I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Disrupted sleep schedule
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about four hours most nights. He wakes up at 3 in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours. I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Work thoughts during downtime
facts.content: Daniel thinks about work even when he is not working. He is at his desk by 7 and still answering messages at 10 at night.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night.

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's diagnosis
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Caring for father's health
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks.

facts.heading: Sole responsibility for care
facts.content: Daniel is the one responsible for all care for his father because his sister lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Guilt about expressing needs
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying he is tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it.

facts.heading: Avoidance coping mechanism
facts.content: Daniel cannot face something. He breathes and looks at people.
facts.evidence: Because I can't face it. That's an important thing to notice.

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests done by his GP. The results were all normal.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests. They were all normal.

facts.heading: GP suggested support
facts.content: The GP suggested Daniel talk to someone. Daniel felt he had no time for it.
facts.evidence: they said I hadn't got time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend booked an appointment for him. She said she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked that, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Girlfriend is patient
facts.content: Claire is patient with Daniel. She makes him tea and does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Girlfriend wearing another hat
facts.content: Daniel sees that Claire is wearing another hat.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's wearing another hat, too.

facts.heading: Girlfriend stops weekend invites
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel if he wants to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: Just stop asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails prevent rest
facts.content: The emails prevent Daniel from saying yes to plans. He will come back to them when he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to underage them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that even rest has a cost.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price? Yeah, exactly.

facts.heading: Stopped running 10k
facts.content: Daniel stopped running 10 kilometers every Saturday morning about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. I ran. 10 kilometers every Saturday morning.

facts.heading: Legs feel like lead
facts.content: Daniel's legs feel like lead now. He has not returned to running.
facts.evidence: My legs feel like lead. I just never went back.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He felt running was the one time nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Relationship with boss Peterson
facts.content: Daniel's boss is Peterson. Peterson sends emails at 11 at night and expects answers before breakfast.
facts.evidence: Peterson. He's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answering emails immediately
facts.content: Daniel answers every email, even when he is in bed. Claire hates this.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of not answering
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that if he doesn't answer, his boss will think he is not committed.
facts.evidence: Then he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: There is a restructuring in the spring, and Daniel is afraid they will let him go.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Ambivalent reaction to job loss
facts.content: Daniel does not know how he would feel if he were let go. He might feel relieved but also horrible about being relieved.
facts.evidence: I don't know. I'd think part of me would be relieved and I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during rest
facts.content: Daniel slept at a colleague or nothing last week and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.
facts.evidence: I slept at a colleague last week or nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Heart palpitations experienced
facts.content: Daniel's heart was going and his hands were shaking during the incident. He thought it was a heart attack but it passed.
facts.evidence: Heart was going and my hands were shaking. I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Previous frightening experience
facts.content: Daniel has experienced frightening events before. This happened once on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: once on a train to Manchester just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that he is losing it. He worries about coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee and wine use
facts.content: Daniel consumes about six cups of coffee daily. He drinks wine in the evenings to switch his head off.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day and I've started having wine in the evenings

facts.heading: Alcohol consumption frequency
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine in the evenings.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Alcohol effect duration
facts.content: The wine helps for about an hour. Daniel wakes up at three anyway.
facts.evidence: It works for an hour. I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Feeling of listing problems
facts.content: Daniel feels like he is listing everything that is wrong with him.
facts.evidence: Feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing thoughts
facts.content: Daniel felt a bit of relief after speaking. He did not realize he was carrying a burden.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of relief, actually. Like putting an angle bad, but I didn't realize I was carrying.

facts.heading: Desire to sleep to cope
facts.content: Daniel thinks that if he could sleep, he could probably cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather's coping style
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything. He just got on with it.
facts.evidence: He never complained about anything. Not once. That's the same. Just get on with it.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there. Daniel thinks he is not weak.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here. That I'm not weak.

facts.heading: Feeling of tiredness
facts.content: Daniel stated he is very tired. He stated he is not weak.
facts.evidence: Just very tired.

facts.heading: Willingness to try small steps
facts.content: Daniel was asked if he would be willing to try something small. He agreed to try something.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with glare.

facts.heading: Proposed evening routine
facts.content: Daniel agreed to fix a time in the evening when he switches off his phone for 20 minutes.
facts.evidence: Fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone, even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Current feeling state
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter. He noted that it is normal to feel shaky after speaking.
facts.evidence: Dired, but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.

facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here.
